description: The six feature-module definitions, a verdict for every module id, resolution of a bundle or a world's list (refusing the unimplemented and port-later ids) and the pause tabs it leaves, proficiency tiers and scores, adaptive difficulty parameters and the quest difficulty adjustment, in integers (src/progression/feature-modules.ts).
comparison: exact, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip

cases.name: definitions: the six module definitions and a verdict for each of the thirteen ids

definitions.description: Track discoverable knowledge entries with mastery progression and spaced repetition

definitions.name: Gamification

definitions.name: Adaptive Difficulty

cases.name: genre: every registry genre, an unknown one and none: the pause tabs a host shows once refused modules are dropped
cases.note: tabsDeclared is what the bundle alone would show; tabs is what shows once resolution drops the refused ids (the language bundle loses its Assessment tab, as assessment is port-later).

cases.name: proficiency: the overall percentage and tier at each edge, the ladder relabelled by a bundle
cases.note: Scores are thousandths of a point on a scale of 5. The tier is judged on the exact mean: 6249 over five dimensions is 24.996 % (Novice), 6250 is 25 % (Apprentice). The language bundle's four labels give four tiers, so 90 % is still B2.

cases.name: difficulty: the tier and the three parameters at each edge, labels from the bundle
cases.note: Score in thousandths of a percent; intensity = score / 100 permille (half up), capped at 1000; hints and assistance its complement.

cases.name: performance: the composite score in permille, part by part
cases.note: success 40 %, objectives 30 %, attempt efficiency (n / total attempts) 20 %, time 10 % ((2000 − mean ratio) × 2 / 3, 500 untimed). No records is 500.
